newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dassault in T$100 mln Taiwan investment.
newsitem.headline: Dassault in T$100 mln Taiwan investment.

text.p: France's Dassault Aviation plans to invest T$100 million in a Taiwan aviation parts maker as part of a deal to help develop the island's fledgling aerospace industry, the economics ministry said on Monday.
Dassault would officially sign a contract on Tuesday with Chuan Feng Co to take a 10 percent, T$100 million stake in the Taiwan firm, the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry said it was the biggest French commercial investment in Taiwan in nearly two years.
Dassault was expected to further expand its Taiwan investments, the statement said.
In July 1996, Dassault signed a contract with the economics ministry to allow domestic firms to make parts for 60 Mirage 2000-5 fighters the island is buying from France.

Under the pact, subcontracts awarded to Taiwan firms would involve the manufacture of spare parts and components, maintenance, aviation software and integrated circuits used in Dassault-made Mirage fighters.
Taiwan has never disclosed the value of the 1992 purchase of 60 Mirage fighters, widely reported to be between US$2 billion and $2.6 billion.
Taiwan's longstanding policy is to ask for 30 percent in offsetting industrial cooperation deals for local firms after making major military purchases.

A Taipei newspaper said on Monday that France would deliver to Taiwan of an initial batch of Mirage 2000-5 fighter jets in April -- a month ahead of schedule -- to avert political frictions at a May summit in China.
The Nationalist-owned Central Daily News did not say how many of the 60 Mirage fighers would be delivered in the first batch.
